title: Upgrade Sprint Campaigns and Checklists
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable sprint playbook CS teams can run to convert mid-market customers from Hosted to either Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) and to sell premium SLA add-ons. The approach is technical-advocacy-led, timed to renewal windows or QBR follow-ups.

When to run:
- Renewal < 90 days and usage trends show predictable growth or sustained high spend
- Latency/cost incidents in last 6 months that created dissatisfaction
- Customer has regulatory/compliance signals (SOC, HIPAA, data residency)

Outcome metrics (success criteria):
- Conversion to Dedicated or Private: goal = 1 signed expansion per sprint (90d target)
- Premium SLA attachments: attach rate >= 20% for eligible accounts
- Time from initial outreach to signed contract: median <= 45 days
- Technical readiness score >= 8/10 at handoff to Onboarding/Delivery

6-week Sprint cadence (templates + checklists)
Week 0: Intake & Prioritization (2 days)
- Owner: AE + CSM + Solutions engineer (SE)
- Tasks: confirm renewal date, current spend and burst patterns, top 5 latency/token cost incidents, compliance checklist (does customer need VPC/HSM?), decision maker map
- Deliverable: one-pager "Opportunity Brief" (1 A4) with impact estimate (monthly token $ delta)

Week 1-2: Technical Qualification & Proof-of-Need (10 working days)
- SE executes lightweight infra audit: peak qps, median p99 latency, KV cache hit rate, sequence length distribution
- Run cost-sensitivity analysis: run a small token-cost simulation comparing Hosted vs Dedicated (config assumptions included)
- Deliverable: Tech Gap Table (items: network egress, VPC peering, encryption, audit logs) + Recommendation (Dedicated vs Private)

Week 3: Executive & Economic Pitching (5 days)
- Prepare a 6-slide QBR addendum: 1) current usage snapshot 2) pain statements 3) economic comparison 4) deployment options & timelines 5) migration risk mitigation 6) proposed next steps and commercial outline
- Finance ops to provide model: 12-month TCO delta + payback period for Dedicated commit
- Deliverable: QBR addendum slide deck + proposed term sheet sketch

Week 4-5: Technical Validation & Pilot (10 days)
- If Dedicated: offer 2-week pilot with reserved pool sizing, SE validates performance on sample workload (customer-supplied prompt set)
- If Private: scope network/workload acceptance tests, propose phased handoff (control plane + runtime sticker)
- Security review checklist executed (IAM, KMS, audit log retention)
- Deliverable: Pilot report with latency/cost delta and go/no-go recommendations

Week 6: Close & Handoff (5 days)
- Final commercial negotiation, legal templates (attachment for SLA add-on), signatures
- Handoff to Delivery: migration runbook, roles/responsibilities, SRE escalation contacts, rollback plan
- Deliverable: Signed MSA/Order + Migration Plan

Qualification checklist (quick scan)
- Average monthly spend > $5k OR peak qps causing consistent throttling
- Need for predictable latency SLA (p99 < X ms requirement)
- Data residency/compliance requirement flagged
- Engineering sponsor identified (name + email)
- Internal billing/finance approver known

Technical gating matrix (SE quick score 1–10)
- Network readiness (VPC, peering, egress): score 1–10
- Data sensitivity & KMS requirements: score 1–10
- Expected throughput & burst profile match: score 1–10
- Observability & tracing requirements: score 1–10
- Migration complexity (custom connectors): score 1–10
- Technical readiness = average; >= 7 recommended for 30-day migration

Objection handling snippets
- "Hosted is cheaper now": compare 12-month TCO + engineering cost of incidents; show predictability of unit cost with Dedicated and caching gains
- "We can’t move data off cloud": outline Private/VPC option, customer-managed KMS, and audit log access
- "Lock-in concerns": explain same API surface, ability to pin model versions, escape hatches and rollbacks in migration runbook

QBR slide checklist (addendum to standard deck)
- Slide 1: Exec summary (impact statement + ask)
- Slide 2: Usage & pain map (charts: tokens by route, p95/p99 latency trends)
- Slide 3: Incident & cost story (top 3 incidents last 6 months + estimated cost)
- Slide 4: Option matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with pros/cons + timeline
- Slide 5: Economic case (TCO, payback, optional SLA pricing)
- Slide 6: Next steps & decision calendar

Sample short outreach email (first contact)
Subject: Quick QBR follow-up — options to reduce token spend & stabilize latency
Hi {{name}},
Thanks for the QBR conversation last week. I pulled a short impact brief showing two options (Dedicated reserved pool or Private VPC) that would reduce token volatility and give a predictable latency SLA. Can we sync 30 min this week to walk through the numbers?
Best,
Maya (CS)

Follow-up email (after pilot)
Subject: Pilot results + recommended next steps
Hi {{name}},
Pilot finished — we saw median p99 latency improvement of {{x}} and an estimated monthly token savings of ${{y}} under the proposed Dedicated commit. Attached is the pilot report and a one-page term sketch. Happy to get legal looped if you want to proceed.
Thanks,
Maya

Renewal tracker (fields suggested)
- account_name | renewal_date | current_product | proposed_product | estimated_delta_monthly_cost | finance_contact | technical_owner | pilot_required?(y/n) | status | next_action | owner | notes
Example row: AcmeCorp | 2025-03-12 | Hosted | Dedicated | 4,200 | finance@acme.com | eng-lead@acme.com | y | pilot-scheduled | send-pilot-setup | Maya | needs HSM for logs

Escalation path (if procurement stalls)
- 1) CSM escalates to AE for pricing flexibility
- 2) AE escalates to Sales Manager for term concessions (max 10% discount without CFO approval)
- 3) Head of CS / Solutions available for exec sponsor call

Operational artifacts to attach when handing over
- Migration runbook (templates for DB dumps, traffic cutover, rollback)
- Pilot report (latency & cost dashboards)
- Security signoff checklist
- Signed commercial attachments and SLA language

Open questions / TODOs
- Create a templated pilot data collection workbook for SEs (action: Evan Li)
- Confirm standard SLA add-on pricing bands (action: Finance — CS-482)
- Draft legal addendum template for Private deployments (action: Legal — planned in JIRA CS-501)

Notes and heuristics
- For customers with highly bursty traffic, emphasize caching strategies and batching first; Dedicated helps but caching often yields >30% token cost savings quickly.
- Use small, measurable pilots (7–14 days) rather than lengthy POCs — reduces time-to-decision.
- Always attach a simple rollback plan to reduce perceived migration risk.
